target_customer: Insurers, MGAs, brokers and risk teams in investment management that process complex multi-document packages
problem: Risk and underwriting teams manually reconcile values across loss runs, bordereaux, policies and data rooms. Parsewise extracts and validates data across documents with traceability to sources.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API with onboarding by plan (Growth, Business, Enterprise)
product_category: Document AI for insurance and risk

founders.name: Max Hofer
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: former Bain consultant.

founders.name: Greg Csegzi
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: experience in life sciences, insurance and manufacturing.

technical_complexity.rationale: Resolving and validating values across many heterogeneous documents with traceability and SOC 2 level controls is harder than single-document extraction, though built on commodity LLMs.

defensibility.rationale: Customer-specific configuration and onboarding create some lock-in, but document AI vendors and foundation model providers can build similar pipelines.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No reporting of a copy or acquisition as of late 2026; a Databricks technology partnership and an OfficeQA Pro benchmark claim appear on company channels.

market_need_then: Insurance and investment teams spend heavy manual effort on document reconciliation; the company cites customers such as Compre for loss runs and bordereaux, self reported.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise and compliance focused; product assistant named Navi

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive coinage near Parse.ly and similar names; no press or community evidence about the brand was found.

pivots.from: Multi-document processing API for pipelines and AI agents
pivots.to: Navi AI assistant focused on insurance, MGAs and brokers
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from YC description versus current site, so treat as a positioning shift.

outcome_analysis: Parsewise, a Spring 2025 YC company from London, is active in late 2026 with no exit or reported shutdown. It has insurance customers named on its own site and claims SOC 2 Type II, a Databricks partnership and a benchmark result. Funding amounts conflict across aggregators, so its financing trajectory is unknown.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators give $2M seed (2025-04, Partech, YC), $500K pre-seed/seed (2025-04 or 2025-06, Network VC, Oxonian, General Advance) and $130K; no primary announcement found, so no rounds recorded. Competitor sources found were undated vendor comparisons, so the list is empty. The pivot entry is an inference from changing descriptions and is undated. Customer logos are self reported.
